chunks: Abu Nasr Ahmad ibn Al-Husayn al-Dhabbi narrated to us, and I had not met anyone more biased (Nasibi) than him, and it was reported regarding his bias that he used to say,

O God, send blessings upon Muhammad alone, and he refrained from sending blessings upon his family. He said: I heard Abu Bakr al-Hammamy al-Farra', one of the tradition narrators, in a place called Sikkat Harb in Nishapur, saying: 'Some people entrusted me with a deposit, so I buried it and forgot its location. When a period of time had passed, the owner of the deposit came to me demanding it, but I did not know its location and was confused. The owner accused me, so I left my house grieving and confused. I saw a group of people heading to the Shrine of Ar-Rida (peace be upon him), so I went with them to the Shrine, visited, and prayed to God to make clear to me the location of the deposit. I saw there, in what the sleeper sees, as if a man came to me and said to me: "You buried the deposit in such and such a place." So I returned to the owner of the deposit and directed him to that place which I had seen in the dream, while I myself did not believe in what I had seen. The owner of the deposit went to that place, dug it up, and extracted the deposit with the seal of its owner intact. After that, the man used to narrate this story to the people and urge them to visit this Shrine, greetings and peace be upon its resident.'

key_terms.فَرْدًا: Alone (referring to Muhammad alone, excluding the family)
key_terms.نَصْب: Bias (specifically against the Ahl al-Bayt, often used for Nasibi)

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the lost deposit and the Shrine of Imam al-Rida in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narrative from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *'Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* illustrates the concept of *karamat* (miracles of the Imams) through a man who, after losing a buried deposit, received a dream revealing its location following a visit to the Shrine of Imam al-Rida in Tus. It underscores the Shia belief in the intercessory power of the Ahl al-Bayt and the spiritual efficacy of *ziyarat* (visitation) for resolving worldly anxieties and gaining divine clarity.
